title: A small first collaboration: Noah's Hope and BDFA

sentences.text: At Noah's Hope, we support families affected by TPP1-related disorders (CLN2 disease).
BDFA supports the wider Batten community; its CLN3 connection is inferred by the atlas rather than explicitly named on its page.
CLN2 and CLN3 both involve material building up in cells' recycling compartments, called lysosomes.
Their symptom similarity is atlas-inferred, with confidence 0.4—below 0.5—not confirmed clinical equivalence.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The International DEM-CHILD Database already collects CLN2 natural-history information about how disease changes over time.
The Batten Disease Clinical Research Consortium (BDCRC) and its longitudinal natural-history study are recorded as CLN3 resources, although the cited wording is Batten-wide.
Could we explore sharing study-design experience, without assuming that access or eligibility carries over?

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether BDCRC accepts CLN2 and whether low tissue TPP1 activity, trunk shaking (truncal titubation), and overshooting eye movements occur in CLN3.
Please review the additional symptom differences flagged for BDCRC before proposing shared assessments.
For any wider Gaucher or Pompe collaboration, check low TPP1 activity, pigment buildup outside nerve cells and trunk shaking rather than treating missing records as absence.
Before considering the Pompe-focused AMDA Research Grant, verify related-condition eligibility, its additional symptom gaps, and differences involving protein misfolding and glycogen breakdown.
Also seek clinician review of possible lysosomal–SNAREopathy symptom confusion and verify community-resource gaps.
Send BDFA one eligibility enquiry this month asking whether the BDCRC longitudinal natural-history study could include people with CLN2.
Do lysosomal and SNAREopathy disorders overlap in symptoms enough to be confused clinically?
Which lysosomal communities lack a verified patient organisation, registry or research group in the atlas?
Dear Batten Disease Family Association team,
I am writing on behalf of Noah's Hope to explore a modest collaboration.
CLN2 and CLN3 share lysosomal material buildup.
Could you help confirm whether the BDCRC longitudinal natural-history study could include CLN2?
We would welcome clarification of eligibility and disease-specific assessments before taking this further.
Thank you for considering this enquiry.
[Your name], on behalf of Noah's Hope
